BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.claim: The deniers, especially Meccan unbelievers, will think at the Hour that they had stayed only a single evening or morning after being warned.
BURSEVI:v10p256/r6.anchor: أي المنكرين وبالفارسية كوييا كفار مكة

BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.claim: Duha is the period from sunrise until noon; the short span refers to part of one day, with evening and morning linked by their belonging to the same day.
BURSEVI:v10p256/r7.anchor: الضحى اسم لما بين إشراق الشمس إلى استواء النهار ثم هي عشى إلى الغداة

QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.claim: The evening or morning may mean the setting of truth’s light in bodies or its rising from the west; witnessing resurrection through unity makes worldly existence seem only imagined.
QASHANI:79:45-46/r2.anchor: وقت غروب نور الحق في الأجساد أو وقت طلوعه من مغربه

QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.claim: Alternatively, the two brief spans are bodily and spiritual worlds, concealed by sensation and intellect; passing both is described as two steps before arrival.
QASHANI:79:45-46/r3.anchor: في عالم الأجسام والاحتجاب بالحس أو في عالم الأرواح والاحتجاب بالعقل

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.claim: The Prophet should not be troubled by demands for the Hour’s timing: only God knows it, the Prophet’s duty is warning, and at its sight people will feel they stayed only a short while.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r4.anchor: The time of arrival of the Day of Judgement is something which only the Almighty knows

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.claim: At Judgment, people will see that their worldly stay seemed no longer than an evening or morning, so its arrival should not be dismissed as distant.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p168/r3.anchor: more than the first or last part of a day

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.claim: Qatada says people regard their worldly stay as short once they witness the afterlife.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p347#3/r1.anchor: قال معمر وقال قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها ﴾ قال استقلوا لما عاينوا الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.claim: The brief-life comparison brings the Hour close: they will think they lived only an afternoon or its morning, with day-end terms joined by expansive إضافة.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p402/r8.anchor: كأنهم يوم يرونها: تقريب وتقرير لقصر مقامهم في الدنيا.

FARRA:v3p234/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p234/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p234/r4.claim: Evening can mean the end and morning the beginning, so Arabic can pair evening with its next morning or morning with its preceding evening.
FARRA:v3p234/r4.anchor: فهذا بين ظاهر من كلام العرب أن يقولوا: آتيك العشية أو غداتها،

FARRA:v3p234/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p234/r5.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
FARRA:v3p234/r5.claim: A poet of Banū ʿUqayl uses ʿashiyyat al-hilāl for the evening of the crescent's setting, supporting the time-pairing idiom.
FARRA:v3p234/r5.anchor: أنشدني بعض بني عقيل: نحن صبحنا عامرا في دارها ... عشية الهلال أو سرارها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.claim: The likeness either confirms the warning that the Hour will arrive swiftly, or answers mockers who impatiently ask when it will come: after the warning they will have waited only briefly.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r1.anchor: إما تقرير وتأكيد لما ينبيء عنه الإنذار من سرعة مجيء المنذر به

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.claim: The compact wording replaces “only an hour of the day, its evening or forenoon”; possessive suffixes rule out imagining an interval from one day's evening until another day's forenoon.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r2.anchor: على ما نقل عن الزمخشري له أصل وهو لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار عشيته أو ضحاه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.claim: Al-Tibi allows evening or forenoon to stand metaphorically for the whole day; adding the pronoun reinforces this and excludes the broader possibility, like saying one saw something with one's own eyes.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r3.anchor: وقال الطيبي إنه من المحتمل أن يراد بالعشية أو الضحى كل اليوم مجازا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.claim: Alusi prefers the less forced explanation of the added pronoun, while allowing it to reinforce the whole-day interpretation too; he takes the interval as worldly life for some and the grave for others.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r4.anchor: ولكن السابق أبعد من التكلف ولا منع من الجمع وزاد الإضافة حسنا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.claim: The context calls for a short stay after the warning or threat, which both makes the warning real and rebuts their impatient challenge; the sentence is circumstantial on one reading and independent on the other.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r5.anchor: اعتبار كونه بعد الإنذار أو بعد الوعيد تحقيقا للإنذار وردا لاستبطائهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.claim: Connecting “what place are you in regarding its reminder?” as a substitute for their question, or as their quoted words, is weak; the direct answer is that the Hour's endpoint belongs to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r6.anchor: ولا يخفى ضعف ذلك وأخراج البزار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet was repeatedly asked about the Hour until 79:43–44 was revealed, after which he stopped asking about it; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r7.anchor: وصححه عن عائشة قالت ما زال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يسأل عن الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.speaker: طارق بن شهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.claim: Tariq ibn Shihab reports that the Prophet often mentioned the Hour until 79:43–44 was revealed and then refrained from mentioning it.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r8.anchor: عن طارق بن شهاب قال كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يكثر ذكر الساعة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر وشيبة وخالد الحذاء وابن هرمز وعيسى وطلحة وابن محيصن وابن مقسم وأبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.claim: These readers, in a report from al-Mundhir, read mundhir with tanwīn and make it govern its object; the construction is original, while genitive attachment can also serve lightness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p38/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وشيبة وخالد الحذاء وابن هرمز وعيسى وطلحة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.claim: The ‘they’ are Quraysh unbelievers, who will see Resurrection and feel they spent only an evening or its dawn on earth; another view places the short stay in their graves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r2.anchor: {كأنهم} يعني كفار قريش {يوم يرونها} يعاينون يوم القيامة {لم يلبثوا} في الدنيا، وقيل: في قبورهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.claim: Al-Farra notes evening has no literal dawn; this is an Arabic expression for the last or first part of a day, as in the comparison to an hour of a day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p331/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: (2) ليس للعشية ضحى، إنما الضحى لصدر النهار، ولكن هذا ظاهر من كلام العرب

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.claim: When they see it, worldly life or their grave-stay seems no longer than an evening or its morning, as in 46:35; evening and morning belong to one day.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r1.anchor: { كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا } في الدنيا أو في القبور. { إلا عشية أو ضحها }

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.claim: A report promises that a reciter of Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt will be held at resurrection only as long as an obligatory prayer before entering Paradise; no grading is stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:46/r2.anchor: من قرأ سورة النازعات كان ممن حبسه الله في القيامة حتى يدخل الجنة قدر صلاة المكتوبة

BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.claim: Qur'anic uses include duha opposite evening, the sun's light brought forth, and a specific time appointed for events; these usages weigh against interpreting it as the whole day.
BINTSHATI:v1p30/r2.anchor: وفي الاستعمال القرآني، نرى القرآن الكريم استعمل الضحى مقابلاً للعشية

NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.claim: People will feel they scarcely remained; this warns worldly people that they soon leave their pleasures as if they stayed only an evening or morning.
NAHHAS:v5p146/r15.anchor: وكان في هذا معنى التنبيه لمن اغتر بالدنيا وسلامته فيها في أنه سيتركها عن قليل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.claim: The name al-Nāziʿāt points to angels extracting souls and then the account of Pharaoh and Moses; al-Sāhirah and al-Ṭāmmah also fit the oath and the surah’s flow.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r2.anchor: وصور ذلك بنزع الأرواح بأيدي الملائكة الكرام ، ثم أمر فرعون اللعين وموسى عليه السلام ، واسمها النازعات واضح في ذلك المرام

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r6.claim: At the Hour, people will think their stay in the world and graves lasted only part of a day: from noon to sunset, or from morning until noon.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.claim: The comparison belittles worldly time against the limitless afterlife; the Prophet likens this world’s share to a finger dipped in the sea and withdrawn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r7.anchor: وهذا تعبير لنا بما نحسه تقريبا لعقولنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.claim: Disbelievers give differing estimates of their stay, but the truth is that their past seems like a brief hour beside the endless future they face.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p321/r8.anchor: على أن الكفار أيضا يستقصرون مدة لبثهم , فكأنهم أصناف : بعضهم يقول : إن لبثتم إلا عشرا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.claim: The comparison recalls the judgment scene where people say they stayed only an hour, or answer that they remained a day or part of one and defer to the counters.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r1.anchor: كأن لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من النهار يتعارفون بينهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.claim: The surah closes by returning from resurrection to its opening, then connects to the next surah through fear and remembrance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r2.anchor: فقد رجع آخرها بالقيامة على أولها , والتف مفصلها بنزع الأنفس اللوامة على موصلها , واتصلت بأول ما بعدها من جهة الخشية والتذكر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.claim: The report that some answer “a day or part of a day” is linked to the question about years in al-Muʾminūn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p322/r3.anchor: كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين قالوا لبثنا يوما أو بعض يوم اسأل العادين

DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p455/r4.claim: Anas transmits a prayer for success that invokes God's mercy, forgiveness, safety, good deeds, Paradise, and deliverance from Hell, and includes the two verses about the briefness of worldly time.

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r4.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r4.claim: Aisha reports that when visiting Bedouins asked about the Hour, the Prophet pointed to the youngest person and said that if he lived a century, their own Hour would have come.

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the Hour's endpoint as God's knowledge and interprets the brief evening and morning as worldly time.
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r6.anchor: ابن المنذر عن ابن جرير في قوله

DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.claim: Qatada says worldly life will seem slight to people when they see the affair of the Hereafter.
DURR-FULL:v8p413/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {كأنهم يوم يرونها}

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.claim: At the Hour's sight, a person will feel that no more than an evening or its morning had passed; الضحى is attached to العشية for brevity as the day's two ends.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p435/r15.anchor: ثم قرب تعالى أمر الساعة بإخباره أن الإنسان عند رؤيته إياها لم يلبث إلا عشية يوم أو بكرته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.claim: Quraysh's unbelievers will feel, on seeing the Resurrection, as if they had remained in worldly life or their graves for only an evening or its first part.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r1.anchor: يعني كفار قريش يوم يرونها أي يعاينون القيامه لم يلبثوا في الدنيا وقيل في قبورهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.claim: The pronouns in ḍuḥāhā refer to al-ʿashiyya, so the phrase means the evening's own early part.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r2.anchor: والهاء والألف في ضحاها عائدان إلى العشية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.claim: The phrase means the evening's ḍuḥā; Arabic can pair evening with its morning-side or morning with its evening-side to refer to the respective ends of a period.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r3.anchor: إلا عشية أو ضحى العشية قال الفراء فإن قيل للعشية ضحى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.claim: A cited poem says they attacked ʿĀmir at evening, at the new moon's setting or its hidden phase, illustrating the idiom's evening expression.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p24#12/r4.anchor: نحن صبحنا عامرا في دارها عشية الهلال أو سرارها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.claim: When raised from their graves, people will consider worldly life so brief it seemed like part of one afternoon or morning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r2.anchor: إذا قاموا من قبورهم إلى المحشر يستقصرون مدة الحياة الدنيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas defines evening as noon to sunset and morning as sunrise to noon.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r3.anchor: قال جويبر، عن الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: {كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها} أما عشية: فما بين الظهر إلى غروب الشمس،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.claim: Qatada says the whole duration of worldly life will seem brief when people behold the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p318/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: وقت الدنيا في أعين القوم حين عاينوا الآخرة.

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.claim: These verses also demonstrate the Resurrection's tremendous condition and many terrors.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r12.anchor: وتدل على عظيم حال القيامة، وكثرة أهوالها

JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.claim: People will regard worldly life as brief when they witness the Resurrection.
JISHUMI:v10p7277/r5.anchor: ومنها: أنهم يستقلون الدنيا عند معاينته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.claim: People seem to have lived in the world—or in the graves—only an evening or its morning; adding the morning to evening marks less than a full day, just an hour of it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p699/r7.anchor: كأنهم لم يلبثوا في الدنيا ، وقيل : في القبور

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.claim: A report promises that whoever recites Surat al-Nazi'at will be held in the grave and at the Resurrection only as long as an obligatory prayer, then enter Paradise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p700/r1.anchor: من قرأ سورة والنازعات كان ممن حبسه الله في القبر والقيامة حتى يدخل الجنة قدر صلاة المكتوبة

SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.claim: ‘Aw duha-ha’ means the bright part of its evening; it figuratively attaches one time expression to another, naming the two ends of the day, and the cadence favors the construction.
SAMIN-DURR:79:46/r1.anchor: أي: ضحى العشية، أضاف الظرف إلى ضمير الظرف الآخر تجوزا واتساعا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.claim: They are disbelievers seeing the afterlife; they feel they stayed in the world only an afternoon or its morning, since worldly life shrinks in retrospect, as in Quran 10:45.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p199#2/r15.anchor: في الدنيا . { إلا عشية } وهي ما بعد الزوال

MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.claim: When people see the Hour, they will think they stayed amid worldly life and pleasure for only an evening from afternoon to sunset or a morning until the sun rises higher.
MUQATIL:79:42-46/r4.anchor: إلا عشية } وهي مابين صلاة العصر وإلى أن تغيب الشمس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.claim: At the Hour, people will think they stayed in this world only an evening or its noon, because the terror makes the duration seem short; this means less than a full day.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r1.anchor: استقلوا مدة لبثهم فى الدنيا لما عاينوا من الهول كقوله لم يلبثوا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.claim: “The noon of the evening” is licensed by the two periods' relation within one day: their stay did not reach an entire day, only one end of it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p316#7/r2.anchor: وإنما صحت اضافة الضحى إلى العشية للملابسة بينهما لاجتماعهما فى نهار واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.claim: The passage answers those who claim the afterlife involves only spiritual comfort or pain without sensation.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r1.anchor: الآية رد على من قال: أحوال الآخرة غير محسوسة، وإنما هي راحة الروح أو تألمها

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r2.claim: The people who see the Hour are disbelievers, who feel their worldly stay was no more than part of a day.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.claim: The phrase means an afternoon, or the morning following that afternoon, minimizing the apparent length of worldly life.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r3.anchor: أي قدر عشية { أو ضحاها } أي أو قدر الضحا الذي يلي تلك العشية، والمراد تقليل مدة الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.claim: They will think they remained in the world for one day only.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r4.anchor: كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا إلا يوما واحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.claim: Alternatively, they mean they stayed in their graves only through an afternoon or its morning, having underestimated it after seeing the terror.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r5.anchor: وقيل: «لم يلبثوا» في قبورهم «إلا عشية أو ضحاها»، وذلك أنهم استقصروا مدة لبثهم

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.claim: Although morning ordinarily precedes afternoon, Arabs may pair one with the other to mean the same day's opposite end, as in customary appointments.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r6.anchor: ولكن أضيف الضحا إلى العشية، وهو اليوم الذي يكون فيه على عادة العرب

QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r7.speaker: بعض بني عقيل
QURTUBI-FULL:79:46/r7.claim: A poem says they attacked at the evening of the new moon or its sirr, meaning the evening's final hidden phase; it supports the idiom.

ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.claim: In ʿashiyyatan aw ḍuḥāhā, the final alif and hāʾ refer to ʿashiyyah: “an evening or its forenoon,” with the forenoon annexed to the evening.
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r2.anchor: هذه الألف والهاء عائدة على (عشية)، المعنى إلا عشية أو ضحاها.

ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.claim: Morning, evening, and forenoon belong to their day: “morning and its evening” is followed by that day’s evening, whereas “evening and its morning” means the following morning.
ZAJJAJ:v5p282/r3.anchor: والغداة والعشي والضحوة والضحى لليوم الذي يكون فيه،

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.claim: When they see what was promised, worldly life will seem to have lasted only an hour, as in 46:35.
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r1.anchor: كأنهم لم يلبثوا في الدنيا إلا ساعة من نهار

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says the final pronoun in duhaha is an additive particle: they stayed only an evening or a morning.
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس : الهاء والألف صلة للكلام

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj understand 'its morning' as the morning of the day whose evening is named; Arabic can say 'evening or its morning.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r3.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : المراد بإضافة الضحى إلى العشية إضافتها إلى يوم العشية

RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.speaker: النحويون
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.claim: The grammarians allow an annexation based on the slightest relation: an earlier morning may be called the morning of its later evening; the ordeal is called evening and relief its morning.
RAZI-FULL:v31p49/r4.anchor: يكفي في حسن الإضافة أدنى سبب

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.claim: The final verses answer disbelievers who taunted the Prophet for not knowing when the Hour would arrive.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r10.anchor: respond to the disbelievers who chided the Prophet for not knowing when the Hour would come

STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.claim: Most commentators say the time in the grave will seem brief before the resurrection and gathering before God.
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r1.anchor: Most commentators say that this verse means that the time in the grave will seem short

STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.claim: Others say earthly life will seem like only an hour compared with the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r2.anchor: Others say the implication is that life on earth will seem as if it were only an hour

STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.claim: Here morning is said to represent worldly life as people see the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:79:46/r3.anchor: morning (ḍuḥā) is said to refer to the time period of the worldly life

ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.claim: Like several other verses, this indicates that earthly time is an illusory concept that loses meaning in the ultimate reality of the hereafter.
ASAD-NOTES:79:46#n19/r1.anchor: a subtle indication of the illusory, earthbound nature of man's concept of "time" - a concept which, we are told, will lose all its meaning

TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.claim: On seeing the Hour, the deniers will feel they spent only an evening or its morning in worldly life; Arabs use morning and evening for the first and last parts of a day.
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r1.anchor: فكذلك قوله: {إلا عشية أو ضحاها} [النازعات: 46] إنما معناها إلا آخر يوم أو أوله

TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says worldly life will seem brief in their eyes when they encounter the afterlife.
TAB-FULL:v24p101#2/r2.anchor: وقت الدنيا في أعين القوم حين عاينوا الآخرة

TABATABAI:79:46/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r5.claim: The comparison means that worldly life until resurrection will seem as brief as one afternoon or its morning, like a portion of one day.
TABATABAI:79:46/r5.anchor: بأن قرب الساعة من حياتهم الدنيا بحيث مثلهم حين يرونها مثلهم لو لبثوا بعد حياتهم في الأرض عشية أو ضحى تلك العشية

TABATABAI:79:46/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46/r6.claim: The “sojourn” is the interval from worldly life to resurrection, meaning the grave period; counting the whole worldly life for judgment supports this reading.
TABATABAI:79:46/r6.anchor: أن المراد باللبث لبث ما بين الحياه الدنيا والبعث أي لبثهم في القبور

TABATABAI:79:46/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:79:46/r7.claim: One alternative makes the sojourn the interval from asking about the Hour until resurrection; the author objects that people witness the interval only at resurrection and that death, not their question, precedes it.
TABATABAI:79:46/r7.anchor: وقيل المراد به اللبث بين حين سؤالهم عن وقتها وبين البعث

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.claim: The author cites 23:114, which asks how many years people remained on Earth, while rejecting worldly life as the meaning of the brief sojourn.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r1.anchor: قال كم لبثتم في الأرض عدد سنين

TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.claim: The Qummi commentary says the period was part of a day.
TABATABAI:79:46#2/r4.anchor: عشية أو ضحاها } قال بعض يوم

TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.claim: “Its forenoon” is annexed to the evening of the same day; morning and evening expressions imply adjoining periods.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r8.anchor: وقوله أو ضحاها أضاف الضحى إلى العشية والغداة والعشي والضحوة والضحي لليوم

TABRISI:79:45-46/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45-46/r14.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:79:45-46/r14.claim: When people see the Resurrection, the world will seem so short that they will think they spent only an afternoon or its morning there.

THALABI:v10p129/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p129/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p129/r1.claim: When people see the Resurrection, they will feel they had remained in the world—or perhaps in their graves—only an evening or its early morning.
THALABI:v10p129/r1.anchor: كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا في الدنيا قيل: في قبورهم، إلا عشية أو ضحاها

THALABI:v10p129/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p129/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v10p129/r2.claim: Al-Farra notes that evening has no literal duha; the phrase is an Arabic way of saying the end or beginning of a day.
THALABI:v10p129/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: ليس للغاشية ضحى إنما الضحى لصدر النهار

THALABI:v10p129/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p129/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p129/r3.claim: A line by a Banu Uqayl poet uses ʿashiyyat al-hilal for the evening when the new moon is hidden.
THALABI:v10p129/r3.anchor: نحن صبحنا عامرا في دارها … جردا تعاطى طرفي نهارها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.claim: The people meant are the disbelievers of Quraysh, and seeing the Resurrection makes worldly life seem very short.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r1.anchor: {كأنهم} يعني كفار قريش. {يوم يرونها} يعاينون القيامة. {لم يلبثوا} في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.claim: They will have spent only part of a day either in their graves or in worldly life, like the last part or beginning of a day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: يقول لم يمكثوا في قبورهم، ولا في الدنيا إلا قدر آخر نهار أو أوله (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.claim: The final hāʾ and alif in ḍuḥāhā are grammatical extensions; the sense is only an evening or morning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r3.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: الهاء، والألف صلة للكلام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.claim: They explain ḍuḥāhā as the morning of the evening's day, like the Arabic expression evening or its next morning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r4.anchor: والعرب تقول: آتيك العشية أو غداتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.claim: When they see what they denied, they will feel as if they had only stayed in the world for an hour before it passed away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p205/r5.anchor: ومعنى الآية: أن ما أنكروه سيرونه حتى كأنهم لم يزالوا فيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.claim: At its sight, people will think they spent only an evening or morning in their graves, underestimating the time because of the terror they see.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:42-46/r4.anchor: { كأنهم يوم يرونها لم يلبثوا } في قبورهم { إلا عشية أو ضحاها } أي: نهارها

ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.claim: At the Hour, worldly life will seem no longer than an evening or its forenoon; life passes quickly, the cautious escape its terrors, and the heedless reach everlasting calamity.
ELMALILI:79:42-46/r6.anchor: Uzun zannedilen dünya ömrü o kadar çabuk geçer

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.claim: After returning to life, people will see how brief worldly life was beside the everlasting afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r1.anchor: İnsanlar, ikinci hayata döndüklerinde ebedî olan âhirete göre geçici olan dünya hayatının ne kadar kısa olduğunu anlayacaklardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.claim: Psychologically, the past seems short because it is finished; the open, uncertain future feels more important and interesting and can cause anxiety.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:46/r2.anchor: Psikolojik olarak insana geçmiş daima kısa bir zamanmış gibi gelir; çünkü geçmiş artık olmuş bitmiştir

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: A question about when something happened can be answered with event-times such as the pilgrims' departure, star-setting, or a person's succession.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: وذلك قولك متى سير عليه ؟ فيقول مقدم الحاج وخفوق النجم وخلافة فلان

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: بني تميم
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: Banū Tamīm allow إذا جاء غد فأتني with كان omitted; its expanded sense refers to whatever state of safety or affliction obtains tomorrow.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: غدا فأتنى وهى لغة بنى تميم

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: The omitted كان is understood from the context and is dropped for ease because كان is frequent and serves as the basic expression for past and future.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: Other frequent expressions also omit understood material, as in ḥīnaʾidhin al-ān and the idiom lā ʿalayka.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: Lā ʿalayka omits lā baʾsa or lā ḍarra because the addressee understands the fixed expression; Sībawayh says this ellipsis is confined to that phrase.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: ولا يكون هذا فى غير لا عليك

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: The explicit إذا كان غدا فأتني is grammatical when prior context has introduced an affair, and this type of ellipsis works with any verb after its overt antecedent.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: لأنك إنما أضمرت بعد ما ذكرت مظهرا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: إذا كان الليل فأتني is not valid in the same way unless night means the entire night or the omitted matter has already been introduced in context.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: فإن قلت إذا كان الليل فأتنى

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: For a particular night or day, sahar and similar temporal names occur only as accusative adverbs; sahar can inflect when indefinite or with the article, and its diminutive is sahīr.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: ومما لا يحسن فيه إلا النصب قولهم سير عليه سحر

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: When denoting the particular day, ḍuḥā and ʿashiyya are adverbial accusatives and do not take genitive in this use, as in the verse's comparison to an evening or its morning.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: Names such as dhāta marratin, buʿaydāta bayn, and bakran are likewise restricted to adverbial accusative in these senses, not ordinary nominal use.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: ذات مرة نصب لا يجوز إلا هذا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: Other specific time expressions, including ḍaḥwa, ʿatma, dhāta yawm, dhāta layl, laylan, and nahāran, behave similarly as adverbs.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: وكذلك سير عليه عتمة إذا أردت

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: Yūnus reports the normal Arabic use of dhā ṣabāḥ like dhāta marratin; Khathʿam has a differing dialect that permits it to be raised.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: لخثعم
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: A Khathʿam speaker uses dhā ṣabāḥ outside the ordinary adverbial pattern, as in a verse permitting nominative case.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: وقال رجل من خثعم ~~PageV01P226 # % عزمت على إقامة

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.claim: A non-inflecting temporal expression cannot be made a raised subject at the start of a sentence unless it is construed as an adverb.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكمتىسيرعليه؟فيقولمقدمالح.anchor: وجميع ما ذكرنا من غير المتمكن إذا ابتدأت اسما لم يجز

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r1.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r1.claim: Al-Khalīl says that words following lā can take the case of their syntactic position rather than the case imposed directly by lā; Dhu al-Rumma's example illustrates this.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r1.anchor: فزعم الخليل ~~رحمه الله أن هذا يجرى

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r2.claim: The same positional case appears in the poetic phrase falsnā bil-jibāli wa-lā al-ḥadīdā, where the poet uses the syntactic position rather than the governing particle.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r3.claim: Sībawayh explains that qalīlun and kathīrun are raised by syntactic position in the expression lā māla lahu.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r4.claim: After lā, as in lā mithlahu rajul, one may follow the syntactic position, follow lā with tanwīn and accusative, or use the construction lā mithlahu rajulan.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r4.anchor: إذا حملته على الموضع كما قال بعض العرب

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r5.speaker: ذو الرمة
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r5.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's line lā amthāluhunna layāliyā supplies a poetic example of the case variation after lā.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r5.anchor: وقال ذو الرمة # % هى الدار إذ مى لاهلك جيرة % ليالى لا أمثالهن لياليا % %

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r6.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r6.claim: Al-Khalīl argues that lā rajul occupies the position of a nominative subject, as shown by lā rajulun afḍalu minka, equivalent to Zayd is better than you.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r6.anchor: وقال الخليل رحمه الله يدلك على أن لا رجل

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r7.speaker: جرير
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r7.claim: Jarīr's lā ka-l-ʿashiyyati zāʾiran wa-mazūran must be accusative because evening cannot be a visitor; an implicit verb such as arā is understood.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r7.anchor: من قبل أن العشية ليست بالزائر وإنما أراد

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r8.claim: In this construction kāf is a preposition, not a noun, with a sense like fī al-yawm; the omitted verb is understood from frequent usage, as in exclamatory expressions.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r8.anchor: فكاليوم كقولك في اليوم لأن الكاف ليست باسم

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r9.claim: In lā ka-l-ʿashiyyati ʿashiyyatan and lā ka-Zaydin rajulun, the second term can be nominative by position because it repeats or classifies the first; lā ka-Zayd means no one like Zayd.

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r10.speaker: امرؤ القيس
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r10.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's phrase wa-lā ka-hādhā alladhī fī al-arḍ maṭlūb is understood as wa-lā shayʾun ka-hādhā, with nominative by position; accusative is also possible.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r10.anchor: قال [ الشاعر ] امرؤ القيس # % ويلمها في هواء الجو طالبة %

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r11.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r11.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r11.claim: The cited mرفad line can be analyzed with an omitted lā aḥad and the following noun related to Zayd, or by analogy with lā māla lahu qalīlan wa-lā kathīran.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r11.anchor: كأنه قال لا أحد كزيد رجلا

SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r12.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r12.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r12.claim: Lā ʿalayka omits an understood noun, meaning lā baʾsa ʿalayka or lā shayʾa ʿalayka, because the expression is frequent.
SIBAWAYH:فمنذلكقولذىالرمة#361/r12.anchor: وإنما يريد لا بأس عليك ولا شئ عليك

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: Hijazi Arabic puts the exception in the accusative after a negative, construing it as a corrective ‘but’: ‘there is no one there but a donkey.’
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.anchor: وهو لغة أهل الحجاز وذلك قولك ما فيها أحد إلا حمارا جاءوا به على معنى

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: Tamim raises the exception, treating أحد as emphatic and the following noun as its replacement: ‘there is no one there but a donkey.’
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.anchor: فيقولون لا أحد فيها إلا حمار أرادوا ليس فيها إلا حمار ولكنه ذكر أحدا

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: A further construal makes the exception the place’s sole inhabitant; Abu Dhuʾayb’s poem calls the echoes of the graves his companions, and other examples identify an exception with the speaker’s defining quality.
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.anchor: وإن شئت جعلته إنسانها قال الشاعر وهو أبو ذؤيب الهذلي

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: When the exception is a verbal noun outside the preceding category, as in ‘his authority is only affectation,’ the construction means ‘but affectation.’
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.anchor: ومن ذلك من المصادر ماله عليه سلطان إلا التكلف

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: In 52:28 the Hijazi accusative treats following الظن as a corrective exception to there being no knowledge.
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.anchor: ما لهم به من علم إلا

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: Tamim raises this construction and treats following الظن, good opinion, or affectation as the relevant knowledge or authority.
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.anchor: هذا كله يجعلونه اتباع الظن علمهم

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: Al-Khalil explains the raised reading by analogy with poetry that calls a painful blow the warriors’ greeting, just as Tamim calls conjecture their knowledge.

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: The exception in 36:43 likewise denotes a mercy from God, not an item in the class of rescuers or cries for help.

SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.claim: Poetic exceptions such as ‘no reproach but the sword’ support the analysis where the exception is identified with the preceding notion, especially when both nouns are definite.
SIBAWAYH:وهولغةأهلالحجازوذلكقولكمافيهاأح.anchor: ما أتاني زيد إلا عمرو وما أعانه إخوانكم إلا إخوانه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.speaker: يونس عن أبي عمرو
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.claim: Yunus reports Abu ʿAmr’s rule, which Sībawayh calls the analogical account: غدوة and بكرة lose tanwin when used as definite names for a time, whether established by context or stated alone.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.anchor: يونس عن أبي عمرو وهو قوله أيضا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.claim: ضحوة and عشية remain indefinite in every case, like صباحا and مساء; context can nevertheless identify them as that day’s morning or evening.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.anchor: فأما ضحوة وعشية فلا يكونان إلا نكرة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.claim: Al-Khalil permits غدوة and بكرة with اليوم, treating them like ضحوة.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.anchor: وزعم الخليل أنه يجوز أن تقول

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.speaker: أبو الخطاب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.claim: Abu al-Khattab heard a trusted Arab use بكرة for an arrival later the same day or the next day; Sībawayh connects this usage with 19:62.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.anchor: وزعم أبو الخطاب أنه سمع من يوثق به من العرب يقول آتيك بكرة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.claim: As an adverb, سحر is indeclinable; with من or عند it takes the article, while its indefinite use is restricted to a specially shifted construction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.anchor: وأما سحر إذا كان ظرفا فإن ترك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالأحيانفيالانصرافوغيرالا.claim: Some Arabs omit tanwin from عشية, as they do from غدوة.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: Time nouns have diminutives such as مغيربان الشمس and عشيان; Arabs also say عشيشية for عشية, construing it through these less regular forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.anchor: فمن ذلك قول العرب في مغرب الشمس مغيربان الشمس وفي العشى آتيك عشيانا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: Al-Khalil derives أصيلالا from أصيلان by replacing its final ن with ل; أصيلانا confirms the underlying form.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.anchor: سألت الخليل عن قولك آتيك أصيلالا فقال إنما هو أصيلان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: Sībawayh reports al-Khalil’s explanation that plurals عشيانات and مغيربانات divide the evening or sunset period into successive parts, each treated as an عشية or مغربان.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.anchor: عشيانات ومغيربانات فقال جعل ذلك الحين أجزاء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: The ordinary diminutives are غدية from غدوة, سحير from سحر, and ضحيا from ضحى; a verse by al-Nābigha al-Jaʿdī attests ضحيا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.anchor: فأما غدوة فتحقيرها عليها تقول غدية

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: Diminutives of time words bring one time nearer another and reduce the interval; they do not mean that the time or a place itself has been made smaller.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.anchor: تحقيرك هذه الأشياء الحين ولكنك تريد أن تقرب حينا من حين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: When these time words are used as personal names, they take the regular diminutive pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.anchor: وجميع ذا إذا سمي به الرجل حقر على القياس

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: Frequent words may have irregular diminutives: إنسان becomes أنيسيان, بنون becomes أبينون, and examples include لييلية and رويجل; names revert to the regular pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.anchor: إنسان تقول أنيسيان وفي بنون أبينون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايحقرعلىغيربناءمكبرهالذ.claim: صبية and غلمة yield أصيبية and أغيلمة on a plural pattern used for فِعال and فَعيل; some Arabs instead use the regular forms صبية and غليمة.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r1.claim: In a form with two hamzas, the hamza before the final one is replaced by ياء; this distinguishes words such as خطايا, with a weaker substituted hamza, from forms whose hamza replaces a radical, such as قضاء.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r1.anchor: ألفا وأبدلوا مكان الهمزة التي قبل الآخر ياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r2.claim: The replacement avoids the weight of two hamzas near two alifs and distinguishes a hamza substituted for an extra letter from one replacing a root consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r2.anchor: همزتان إحداهما بدل من زائدة لأنها أضعف يعني همزة خطايا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r3.claim: In lightened speech hamza may become the matching long vowel: alif after fatḥa, yāʾ after kasra, or wāw after ḍamma; this is learned from usage, not a rule applied to every word.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r3.anchor: تبدل مكانها الألف إذا كان ما قبلها مفتوحا والياء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r4.claim: Poetic necessity can extend this replacement systematically; al-Farazdaq uses an alif because the intermediate hamza pronunciation would break the meter.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r5.claim: The Huthayl forms سلت and يسال are not ordinary in the poets’ dialects, though Sībawayh was told that سلت تسال is a dialect.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r6.claim: The forms نبي and برية take hamza replacement by lexical convention, not as a general rule; some Hijazi speakers who normally articulate hamza retain it in نبي and بريئة, a rare and disfavored usage.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r6.anchor: وقالوا نبي وبرية فألزمها أهل التحقيق البدل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r7.claim: Some speakers replace an open hamza at a word boundary, as in أونت for أو أنت and أبو يوب for أبو أيوب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r7.anchor: العرب منها من يقول في أو أنت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r8.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r8.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r8.claim: Inside a word, some speakers delete hamza in سوأة and موأله, and in حوأب say حوب; a radical hamza behaves like a root consonant.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r8.anchor: وإن كانت في كلمة واحدة نحو سوأة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r9.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r9.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r9.claim: Speakers simplify hamza in clusters of wāws, yāʾs, and kasras, as in أحلبني بلك and أرمي مك, to avoid difficult sequences.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r10.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r10.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r10.claim: Some speakers delete hamza in forms such as أنا ذو نسه and يجيك ويسوك; before wāw or yāʾ they avoid ḍamma, but may retain kasra in يرم خوانه.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/r10.anchor: يحذف الهمزة ويكره الضم مع الواو والياء

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r1.claim: A poet names the camel's load as ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib but means ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās, substituting the father for the son.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r1.anchor: أراد: (عبد الله بن عباس) فذكر أباه مكانه.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r2.claim: Al-Ṣaltān intended to say Jarīr surpassed al-Farazdaq in poetry but used their grandfathers' names to fit the verse.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r2.anchor: أراد: «أرى جريرا بذ الفرزدق شعره» فلم يمكنه فذكر جده.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r3.speaker: ابن الكلبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r3.claim: Ibn al-Kalbī identifies the person called al-Ḥārithiyyūn as Yazīd ibn Hubayr; the poet used the name under metrical pressure.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r3.anchor: قال ابن الكلبي: هو (يزيد بن هوبر) فاضطر.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r4.claim: Aws meant 'son of Ḥudhaym,' a pre-Islamic physician, but omitted son to satisfy the line.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r4.anchor: أراد: (ابن حذيم) وهو طبيب كان في الجاهلية:

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r5.claim: Ibn Mayyādah meant two ibexes on each side, but his wording gives one ibex on each side under poetic constraint.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r5.anchor: أراد: وعلين من كل جانب، فلم يمكنه فقال: ووعل.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r6.claim: Abū al-Najm calls the camel's sire her maternal cousin, substituting one kinship term for another.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r7.claim: A poet says Christians killed the Messiah but means the Jews.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r7.anchor: وقال آخر : مثل النصارى قتلوا المسيح أراد: اليهود:

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r8.claim: Yalab is leather straps worn beneath helmets; the quoted line mistakes or treats them as iron.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r8.anchor: واليلب: سيور تجعل تحت البيض، فتوهمه حديدا.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r9.claim: Ruʾbah's phrase 'silver or sulfur gold' is listed as another inversion or substitution in poetic wording.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r9.anchor: وقال رؤبة : أو فضة أو ذهب كبريت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r10.claim: Abū al-Najm reverses the relation in 'like lightning's gleam in its deceptive lightning' for 'the deceptive gleam of its lightning.'

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r11.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r11.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r11.claim: The poet intended 'someone to rely on' but reversed the relation as 'someone upon whom to rely.'
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p127/r11.anchor: أراد: إن لم يجد يوما من يتكل عليه.

NASHR:v1p274#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p274#2/r1.claim: He defines large assimilation as merging two moving letters, whether identical, homogeneous, or close; small assimilation starts with a quiescent first letter.
NASHR:v1p274#2/r1.anchor: (فالكبير) ما كان الأول من الحرفين فيه متحركا، سواء أكانا مثلين أم جنسين أم متقاربين

NASHR:v1p274#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p274#2/r2.claim: Large assimilation is named for its frequency, the greater impact of first making a moving letter quiescent, its difficulty, or its inclusion of three letter relationships.
NASHR:v1p274#2/r2.anchor: وسمي كبيرا لكثرة وقوعه، إذ الحركة أكثر من السكون. وقيل: لتأثيره في إسكان المتحرك قبل إدغامه

NASHR:v1p274#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p274#2/r3.claim: Abu Amr is the best-known and especially associated imam for large assimilation, though it is also transmitted from al-Hasan al-Basri, Ibn Muhaysin, al-Aʿmash, Talha, ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar, and others; its purpose is ease.
NASHR:v1p274#2/r3.anchor: والمختص به من الأئمة العشرة هو أبو عمرو بن العلاء وليس بمنفرد به، بل قد ورد أيضا عن الحسن البصري

NASHR:v1p274#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
NASHR:v1p274#2/r4.claim: Abu Amr says assimilation is ordinary Arabic speech; Ibn al-Jazari adduces poetry, including a line by ʿAdi ibn Zayd, as evidence for this usage.
NASHR:v1p274#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: الإدغام كلام العرب الذي يجري على ألسنتها، ولا يحسنون غيره

NASHR:v1p274#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274#2/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p274#2/r5.claim: Several earlier manuals omit large assimilation entirely, including works by Abu ʿUbayd, Ibn Mujahid, Makki, al-Talamanki, Ibn Sufyan, and others.
NASHR:v1p274#2/r5.anchor: منهم من لم يذكره ألبتة كما فعل أبو عبيد في كتابه، وابن مجاهد في سبعته

NASHR:v1p274#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p274#2/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p274#2/r6.claim: Other authorities included it as one of two options for Abu Amr, fully across his transmission routes; this excerpt ends before it names that group.
NASHR:v1p274#2/r6.anchor: ومنهم من ذكره في أحد الوجهين، عن أبي عمرو بكماله من جميع طرقه

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r1.claim: Al-Bāqillānī adduces Abu Nuwās’s coarse tribal insults and bodily language as further evidence of jarring passages in celebrated poetry.
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r1.anchor: لا حميري وفي ولا عدس ولا است عير يحكها الثفر

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r2.claim: Such roughness is not unique to Abu Nuwās: al-Aʿshā also supplies strained poetic examples.
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r2.anchor: ولم يقع مثل ذلك له وحده فقد قال الأعشى

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r3.claim: Al-Bāqillānī says the words shāw, mashl, shalūl, shalshal, and shawl all have one meaning.

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r4.claim: Zuhayr likewise places a poor, obscure line in a poem that also contains the admired line about wheat shoots growing from their stalks and palms from their native ground.
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r4.anchor: كيف يقول هذا في قصيدة يقول فيها وهل ينبت الخطى إلا وشيجه وتغرس إلا في منابتها النخل

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r5.claim: In al-Ṭirmaḥ’s line, al-sibantāh means a strong she-camel; al-kirāḍ is the stallion’s fluid, which she expels with urine without retaining it or conceiving, weakening her; al-māʾir means flowing.
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r5.anchor: السبنتاة الناقة الصلبة والكراض ماء الفحل أسالت ماء الفحل مع البول فلم تعقد عليه ولم تحمل فتضعف والمائر السائل

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r6.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r6.speaker: قائل
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r6.claim: A hypothetical critic accuses al-Bāqillānī of unfairness to Imruʾ al-Qays, whose poetry varies between smooth and harsh, gentle and rough, wild and tame; the critic values even, tightly woven speech.
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r6.anchor: فإن قال قائل أجدك تحاملت على امرئ القيس ورأيت أن شعره يتفاوت بين اللين والشراسة وبين اللطف والشكاسة

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r7.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r7.speaker: قائل
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r7.claim: The critic says al-Buḥturī outstrips others in this field and that writers rank his speech above all others.
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r7.anchor: وأنت تجد البحتري يسبق في هذا الميدان ويفوت الغاية في هذا الشان وأنت ترى الكتاب يفضلون كلامه على كل كلام

BAQILLANI:v1p212/r8.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r8.speaker: قائل
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r8.claim: The critic also praises Abū Nuwās for splendid wording and subtle meaning, admired by learned people and ranked above other poets by witty connoisseurs.
BAQILLANI:v1p212/r8.anchor: وكذلك تجد لأبي نواس من بهجة اللفظ ودقيق المعنى ما يتحير فيه أهل الفضل ويقدمه الشطار والظراف على كل شاعر

BURHAN:v3p6#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p6#2/r1.speaker: الفرزدق
BURHAN:v3p6#2/r1.claim: Al-Farazdaq uses the dual المربدان although al-Zarkashi says Basra had only one Mirbad; the text also cites الرقمتين and المكتين as place-name duals.

BURHAN:v3p6#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p6#2/r2.speaker: جرير
BURHAN:v3p6#2/r2.claim: Jarir's الديرين is understood as Dair al-Walid, put in the dual by reference to the surrounding area.

BURHAN:v4p39/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p39/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p39/r9.claim: ضحاها means the forenoon of that same day; al-Zarkashi says the short part stands for the whole.
BURHAN:v4p39/r9.anchor: أي ضحى يومها فدل بالجزء على الكل

BURHAN:v4p39/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p39/r10.speaker: عز الدين
BURHAN:v4p39/r10.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam says adding ضحى to the day of عشية makes the two spans comparable, preserving the contrast between a long and short stay; without it, a long-day forenoon could equal a short-day evening.
BURHAN:v4p39/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين وإنما أضاف الضحى إلى نهار العشية لأنه لو أطلقها من غير إضافة لم يحسن الترديد

ITQAN:v2p549/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p549/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p549/r8.claim: In “an evening or its morning,” the pronoun refers to the day associated with the evening, because an evening itself has no morning.
ITQAN:v2p549/r8.anchor: وقد يعود الضمير على ملابس ما هو له نحو ﴿ إلا عشية أو ضحاها ﴾ أي ضحى يومها لا ضحى العشية نفسها لأنه لا ضحى لها

ITQAN:v4p438/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p438/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p438/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a stopped report for difficult childbirth: verses written on paper and given to drink include the verse about the short stay and another about the promised punishment seeming brief.
ITQAN:v4p438/r5.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في الدعوات عن ابن عباس موقوفا في المرأة يعسر عليها ولادها قال يكتب في قرطاس ثم تسقى

ITQAN:v4p438/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p438/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p438/r10.claim: Al-Suyuti says these are the non-fabricated reports and reports from Companions and Successors that he found on Qur'anic special properties.
ITQAN:v4p438/r10.anchor: فهذا ما وقفت عليه في الخواص من الأحاديث التي لم تصل إلى حد الوضع ومن الموقوفات عن الصحابة والتابعين

RUMMANI:v1p94/r1.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r1.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p94/r1.claim: Rummani defines harmony as balanced arrangement of letters and distinguishes dissonant composition, middle harmony, and the highest harmony.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r1.anchor: التلاؤم نقيض التنافر , والتلاؤم تعديل الحروف في التأليف , والتأليف على ثلاثة أوجه:

RUMMANI:v1p94/r2.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r2.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p94/r2.claim: The Qur’an as a whole occupies the highest tier of harmonious composition, distinguishable on close consideration from all other speech.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r2.anchor: والمتلائم في الطبقة العليا القرآن كله , وذلك بين لمن تأمله.

RUMMANI:v1p94/r3.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r3.speaker: ذكروا
RUMMANI:v1p94/r3.claim: Some attribute the قبر حرب line to jinn: its consonant discord makes it difficult to recite three times without stumbling.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r3.anchor: وذكروا أن هذا من أشعار الجن لأنه لا يتهيأ لأحد أن ينشده ثلاث مرات

RUMMANI:v1p94/r4.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r4.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p94/r4.claim: An unnamed poet’s verse about being struck by love illustrates the middle, still pleasing level of harmonious composition.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r4.anchor: وأما التأليف المتلائم في الطبقة الوسطى - وهو من أحسنها - فكقول الشاعر:

RUMMANI:v1p94/r5.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r5.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p94/r5.claim: People differ in their sensitivity to harmony and dissonance by natural temperament, like their differing ability to hear sound meter or distinguish forms and characters.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r5.anchor: وبعض الناس أشد إحساسا بذلك وفطنة من بعض

RUMMANI:v1p94/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r6.speaker: الخليل
RUMMANI:v1p94/r6.claim: Al-Khalil explains dissonance as either excessive distance or excessive closeness between letters; both impede the tongue, while moderation makes speech easy.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r6.anchor: ما ذكره الخليل من البعد الشديد أو القرب الشديد

RUMMANI:v1p94/r7.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r7.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p94/r7.claim: Harmony pleases the ear, eases pronunciation, and helps the mind accept meaning through attractive form and indication.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r7.anchor: والفائدة في التلاؤم حسن الكلام في السمع

RUMMANI:v1p94/r8.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p94/r8.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p94/r8.claim: The same meaning resembles a book read in beautiful or ugly handwriting: its image varies, and that variation affects reception.
RUMMANI:v1p94/r8.anchor: ومثل ذلك مثل قراءة الكتاب في أحسن ما يكون من الخط والحروف

DAMGHANI:v1p285/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r10.claim: Ḍuḥā can mean the first part of the day, when the sun has risen; the comparison in this verse contrasts it with evening.
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r10.anchor: الثاني الضحى ترجل النهار او ساعة منه قوله تعالى في سورة الضحى والضحى والليل اذا سجى يعني اول ساعة من النهار

DAMGHANI:v1p285/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r17.claim: The seven senses listed for ḍarar are affliction and severity, drought, terrors, illness, decrease, hunger, and harm itself.
DAMGHANI:v1p285/r17.anchor: ض ر ر على سبعة اوجه البلاء والشدة قحط المطر الاهوال المرض النقص الجوع الضر بعينه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r1.claim: Ḍuḥā is the early day as sunlight spreads and reaches its full appearance; its root sense is appearing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r1.anchor: الضحى : صدر النهار في وقت انبساط الشمس ، وهو حالة كمال الشمس في ظهورها . والأصل فيه الظهور

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r2.claim: Arabic usage calls an action done openly or visibly ضاحيا or ضاحية; exposure to the sun is expressed with ضحي or ضحى.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r2.anchor: ويقال : فعل الأمر ضاحيا وضاحية ، أي : ظاهرا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r3.claim: The sacrificial animal is called أضحية because it is slaughtered on Eid day around forenoon.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r3.anchor: وسميت الأضحية : لأنها تذبح يوم العيد عند الضحى

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r4.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r4.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī lists four forms for the sacrificial animal and their plurals, and describes a bright, cloudless night as إضحيانة or ضحياء.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r4.anchor: قال الأصمعي : وفيها أربع لغات : أضحية ( وإضحية والجمع أضاحي ، وضحية والجمع ضحايا ، وأضحاة والجمع أضحى ، وليلة ) إضحيانة وضحياء مضيئة لا غيم فيها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r5.claim: ضاحية can mean the prominent outskirts of a town.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r6.claim: One Qur'anic sense is the time of forenoon, including the phrase ضحاها in 79:46.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p399#2/r6.anchor: أحدها : وقت الضحى . ومنه قوله تعالى في طه : ﴿ وأن يحشر الناس ضحى ﴾ ، وفي النازعات : ﴿ لم يلبثوا إلا عشية أو ضحاها ﴾
